newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Surgeon General Koop denounces tobacco deal.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Surgeon General Koop denounces tobacco deal.

text.p: Former Surgeon General C. Everett Koop said Thursday he opposes a proposed deal that would settle massive litigation against tobacco companies.
"I would oppose it," he said on ABC Television's "This Morning America" program. "I think it's unconstitutional."
He scoffed at reports that the tobacco companies were offering $300 billion over 25 years to settle law suits brought against them for deaths of smokers.
"That's $28,000 per life lost," he said. "I think that's a paltry sum."

Koop, who became a leading anti-smoking spokesman when he served as former President Bush's Surgeon General, said he would like to participate in the talks between the tobacco industry and state attorneys general.
